recipes.name: Omurice
recipes.description: Japanese omelette rice with ketchup heart
instructions: Cook rice and season with soy sauce.
Beat eggs with salt and pepper.
Melt butter in pan and pour egg mixture, swirling to make thin omelette.
Place rice in center and fold egg around it.
Top with ketchup heart.
tips: Use day-old rice for best texture.
Low heat prevents the egg from overcooking.

recipes.name: Cacio e Pepe
recipes.description: Roman pasta with pecorino and black pepper
instructions: Cook pasta in well-salted water.
Toast cracked pepper in dry pan.
Reserve 1 cup pasta water.
Mix cheeses with pasta water into a sauce.
Toss pasta with sauce and pepper.
tips: The pasta water starch is key.
Add cheese off the heat to avoid clumping.

recipes.name: Sopa de Fideo
recipes.description: Mexican noodle soup with tomato broth
instructions: Blend tomatoes, onion, and garlic.
Toast fideo in oil until golden.
Add blended tomato and cook 2 minutes.
Add broth and simmer 10 minutes.
tips: Toasting the noodles first adds nutty depth.
Serve with lime and queso fresco.

recipes.name: Gyudon
recipes.description: Beef bowl with onions and egg
instructions: Slice onion and cook in dashi.
Add soy sauce, mirin, and sugar.
Add beef and cook until done.
Serve over rice.
tips: Freeze beef slightly to slice thinly.
A raw egg yolk on top is traditional.

recipes.name: Carbonara
recipes.description: Roman pasta with egg, guanciale, pecorino
instructions: Render guanciale in pan until crispy.
Cook pasta and reserve water.
Whisk eggs with cheese.
Off heat, combine pasta with guanciale.
Add egg mixture and toss, adding water to loosen.
tips: Never add cream — it's not authentic.
Work quickly off the heat so eggs don't scramble.

recipes.name: Tacos al Pastor
recipes.description: Marinated pork tacos with pineapple
instructions: Soak chiles and blend into marinade with achiote.
Marinate pork for at least 2 hours.
Grill or pan-sear pork until charred.
Slice thin and serve on tortillas with pineapple, onion, and cilantro.
tips: Achiote gives the signature red color.
Char the pineapple for added sweetness.

recipes.name: Blue-Ribbon Chocolate Chip Cookies
recipes.description: The original Mrs. Fields signature cookie — buttery, loaded with chips, perfectly chewy with crisp golden edges.
ingredients: 1 cup dark brown sugar, firmly packed
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda and salt; mix well with a wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl blend sugars with an electric mixer at medium speed.
Add butter and mix to form a grainy paste, scraping down sides of the bowl.
Add eggs and vanilla extract; mix at medium speed until just blended. Do not overmix.
Add the flour mixture and chocolate chips; blend at low speed until just mixed. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoons onto an ungreased cookie sheet, 2 inches apart.
Bake 22–24 minutes or until golden brown.
Transfer cookies immediately to a cool surface with a spatula.
tips: Baking at 300°F rather than 375°F keeps cookies soft and chewy.
Do not overmix after adding flour or cookies will be tough.
Drop dough onto the sheet — resist flattening or shaping.

recipes.name: Soft and Chewy Peanut Butter Cookies
recipes.description: Thick, soft peanut butter cookies with a classic fork crisscross. Variation: add 2 cups chocolate chips.
ingredients: 1½ cups dark brown sugar, firmly packed
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda and salt; mix well with a wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl blend sugars with an electric mixer at medium speed.
Add butter and mix to form a grainy paste, scraping down sides of bowl.
Add eggs, peanut butter and vanilla; mix at medium speed until light and fluffy.
Add flour mixture; mix at low speed until just mixed. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoons onto ungreased cookie sheet, 1¼ inches apart.
With a wet fork, gently press a crisscross pattern on top of each cookie.
Bake 18–22 minutes until cookies are slightly brown along edges.
Transfer cookies immediately to cool surface with a spatula.
tips: Dip fork in water between cookies to prevent sticking.
For a chocolate variation, fold in 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips with the flour.

recipes.name: Oatmeal Raisin Chews
recipes.description: Old-fashioned oatmeal cookies with a hint of honey, plump raisins, and optional walnuts.
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda, salt and oats; mix well with a wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl blend sugars with an electric mixer at medium speed.
Add butter and mix to form a grainy paste; scrape down sides of bowl.
Add honey, vanilla and eggs; mix at medium speed until light and fluffy.
Add the flour mixture, raisins and walnuts; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoons onto ungreased cookie sheets, 1½ inches apart.
Bake 22–24 minutes or until cookies are light golden brown.
Immediately transfer cookies with a spatula to a cool flat surface.
tips: Honey adds extra chew and moisture.

recipes.name: Butterscotch Pecan Cookies
recipes.description: Rich brown sugar cookies crowned with a whole pecan and finished with a buttery caramel glaze.
ingredients: 1¼ cups dark brown sugar, firmly packed
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda and salt; mix well with a wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl beat sugar and butter with an electric mixer; mix to form a grainy paste, scraping down sides.
Add eggs and vanilla; beat at medium speed until soft.
Add flour mixture and chopped pecans; mix at low speed until just combined. Do not overmix.
Drop dough by rounded tablespoons 2 inches apart onto ungreased cookie sheets.
Place one whole pecan in the center of each cookie.
Bake 23–25 minutes or until edges begin to brown lightly; transfer to cool flat surface.
Prepare caramel glaze: melt caramels with cream in a small saucepan over low heat; stir until smooth.
Drizzle cooled cookies with caramel glaze using a spoon or fork.
tips: For authentic butterscotch flavor, substitute the vanilla with an equal amount of scotch whiskey.
Make sure cookies are fully cooled before glazing.

recipes.name: Malted Milk Cookies
recipes.description: Milk chocolate chip cookies with a secret ingredient — malted milk powder — for a deep, nostalgic flavor.
ingredients: ¾ cup plain malted milk powder
½ cup light brown sugar, firmly packed
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, malted milk powder, baking soda and salt; mix well with a wire whisk; set aside.
Blend sugars in a large bowl using an electric mixer at medium speed.
Add butter; mix, occasionally scraping down sides of bowl.
Add eggs, vanilla and condensed milk; beat at medium speed until light and fluffy.
Add flour mixture and chocolate chips; blend at low speed until just combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoons onto ungreased cookie sheets, 2 inches apart.
Bake 24–25 minutes until cookies are slightly brown along edges.
Transfer cookies immediately to cool surface with a spatula.
tips: Malted milk powder is found in the baking aisle near hot cocoa mixes.

recipes.name: Mocha Chunk Cookies
recipes.description: Dark chocolate cookies with a punch of coffee liqueur and big chunks of semisweet chocolate.
ingredients: ½ cup dark brown sugar, packed
2 cups (10 oz) semisweet chocolate bar, coarsely chopped
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, cocoa, baking soda and salt; mix well with a wire whisk; set aside.
In a small bowl dissolve coffee crystals in coffee liqueur; set aside.
In a large bowl blend sugars with an electric mixer at medium speed.
Add butter; mix to form a grainy paste; scrape down sides of bowl.
Add eggs and dissolved coffee; beat at medium speed until smooth.
Add flour mixture and chocolate chunks; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheets, 2 inches apart.
Bake 23–25 minutes; immediately transfer cookies with a spatula to a cool flat surface.
tips: French roast or espresso crystals intensify the mocha flavor.

recipes.name: Chocolate Mint Cookies
recipes.description: Deep chocolate cookies studded with mint chocolate chips — crisp edges, soft centers.
ingredients: ¾ cup light brown sugar, packed
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda, salt and cocoa powder; mix well with a wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl blend sugars with an electric mixer at medium speed.
Add butter; beat to form a grainy paste; scrape sides of bowl.
Add eggs and mint extract; beat at medium speed until light and fluffy.
Add flour mixture and mint chips; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Drop dough by rounded tablespoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheets, 1½ inches apart.
Bake 19–21 minutes; immediately transfer cookies with a spatula to a cool flat surface.
tips: Use pure mint extract, not peppermint oil, for a smoother flavor.

recipes.name: Double-Rich Chocolate Cookies
recipes.description: Intensely chocolatey cookies with both cocoa powder and chocolate chips — for serious chocolate lovers.
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda, salt and cocoa powder; mix well with a wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl blend sugars with an electric mixer at medium speed.
Add butter; beat to form a grainy paste; scrape down sides of bowl.
Add eggs and vanilla; beat at medium speed until light and fluffy.
Add flour mixture and chocolate chips; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Drop dough by rounded tablespoons onto ungreased cookie sheets, 1½ inches apart.
Bake 21–23 minutes; immediately transfer cookies with a spatula to a cool surface.
tips: Use Dutch-process cocoa for a richer, darker result.

recipes.name: Chocolate-Glazed Shortbread Cookies
recipes.description: Classic buttery shortbread cut into shapes and half-dipped in silky chocolate glaze.
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F.
Blend butter until smooth in a large bowl using an electric mixer at medium speed.
Slowly blend in confectioners' sugar; scrape down sides; add vanilla and combine thoroughly.
Add flour; mix at low speed until well blended.
Divide dough into two pieces; flatten each into a disk; wrap in plastic; refrigerate until firm, about 1 hour.
On a floured board roll out disks to ¼ inch thickness; cut with floured cookie cutters.
Bake on ungreased cookie sheets 16–18 minutes; do not let cookies brown; transfer immediately to cool surface.
Prepare glaze: heat cream until scalded; remove from heat; stir in chocolate chips and corn syrup; cover 15 minutes.
Gently mix glaze with a small wire whisk until smooth without creating bubbles.
Dip half of each cooled cookie into the glaze; transfer to waxed paper; refrigerate 10 minutes to set.
tips: Dough must be well-chilled before rolling or it will stick.
Work quickly when dipping — the glaze firms fast.

recipes.name: Almond Crunch Cookies
recipes.description: Delicate almond balls rolled in sliced almonds and drizzled with chocolate glaze — elegant and crunchy.
ingredients: ½ cup almonds, ground in blender
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
In a medium bowl blend butter and sugar with an electric mixer until grainy; scrape down sides.
Add egg and almond extract; beat at medium speed until light and fluffy.
Add ground almonds and flour; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Form dough into 1½-inch balls; roll each ball in sliced almonds until fully coated.
Place balls on ungreased cookie sheets, 2 inches apart.
Bake 15–18 minutes or until slightly brown along edges; transfer to cool surface on waxed paper.
Prepare glaze: scald cream; remove from heat; stir in chocolate chips and corn syrup; cover 15 minutes; mix gently until smooth.
When completely cool, drizzle cookies with warm glaze or dip half into glaze; refrigerate until set.
tips: Handle dough as little as possible for lighter cookies.

recipes.name: Creamy Lemon Macadamia Cookies
recipes.description: Cream cheese-enriched lemon cookies loaded with whole macadamia nuts — tangy, rich, and tender.
ingredients: 1½ cups (7 oz) whole macadamia nuts, unsalted
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda and salt; mix well with a wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl blend sugars with an electric mixer at medium speed.
Add butter and cream cheese; mix to form a smooth paste.
Add egg and lemon extract; beat at medium speed until light and soft; scrape down sides of bowl.
Add flour mixture and macadamia nuts; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoons onto ungreased cookie sheets, 2 inches apart.
Bake 23–25 minutes; immediately transfer with a spatula to a cool flat surface.
tips: Cream cheese keeps these cookies unusually moist for days.

recipes.name: Pumpkin Spice Cookies
recipes.description: Soft, cakey spiced cookies with real pumpkin, raisins, and walnuts — a fall favorite.
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda, salt and pumpkin pie spice; mix well with a wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl blend sugars with an electric mixer at medium speed.
Add butter; beat to form a grainy paste; scrape sides of bowl.
Add egg, pumpkin and vanilla; beat at medium speed until light and fluffy.
Add flour mixture, raisins and walnuts; blend at low speed until combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoons onto ungreased cookie sheets, 2 inches apart.
Bake 22–24 minutes until slightly brown along edges; transfer immediately to a cool surface.
tips: Freshly cooked or canned pumpkin both work well.

recipes.name: Chocolate Raisin Cookies
recipes.description: Chocolate cookies made with melted unsweetened chocolate, plump raisins, and semisweet chips.
ingredients: 1 cup dark brown sugar, firmly packed
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a double-boiler over hot but not boiling water, melt ½ cup butter and the unsweetened chocolate; remove from heat; set aside.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda and salt; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl blend sugars with electric mixer at medium speed until fluffy.
Add remaining ½ cup butter; mix to form a grainy paste, scraping down sides.
Add eggs and vanilla; beat at medium speed until light and fluffy; add melted chocolate and blend.
Add flour mixture, raisins and chocolate chips; blend at low speed until just combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoons onto ungreased baking sheets, 2 inches apart.
Bake 20–22 minutes; transfer to cool flat surface immediately.
tips: Let the melted chocolate cool a few minutes before adding to the batter.

recipes.name: Lemon Poppy Seed Cookies
recipes.description: Bright lemon cookies with poppy seeds and a hint of coriander — light and delicately crunchy.
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda, lemon zest, coriander and poppy seeds; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl cream butter and sugar with electric mixer at medium speed to form a grainy paste.
Scrape down sides; add egg yolks, whole egg and lemon extract; beat until light and fluffy.
Add flour mixture; mix at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoons onto ungreased cookie sheets, 2 inches apart.
Bake 23–25 minutes until slightly brown along edges; transfer immediately to a cool surface.
tips: Fresh lemon zest makes a noticeable difference over bottled extract alone.

recipes.name: Carrot Fruit Jumbles
recipes.description: Wholesome oatmeal cookies packed with grated carrot, crushed pineapple, and walnuts.
ingredients: ¾ cup dark brown sugar, packed
½ cup crushed pineapple, well drained
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda, baking powder, cloves, cinnamon, salt and oats; mix well; set aside.
In a large bowl blend sugars with electric mixer; add butter; mix to form a grainy paste; scrape down sides.
Add eggs and vanilla; beat at medium speed until light and fluffy.
Add carrots, pineapple and nuts; blend until combined (batter will appear lumpy).
Add flour mixture; blend at low speed until just combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded teaspoons onto ungreased baking sheets, 1½ inches apart.
Bake 13–15 minutes — do not brown; transfer immediately with a spatula to a cool flat surface.
tips: Drain pineapple very well or batter will be too wet.

recipes.name: Kids Bake 'Em Cookies
recipes.description: Honey-sweetened chocolate chip cookies designed to be easy enough for kids to make from scratch.
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a small bowl combine flour, baking soda and salt; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
In a medium bowl blend butter, sugar and honey with an electric mixer at medium speed until light and soft; scrape sides.
Add flour mixture and chocolate chips; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Drop dough by rounded teaspoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheets, 1½ inches apart.
Bake 18–20 minutes or until light golden brown.
Immediately transfer cookies with a spatula to a cool flat surface.
tips: Honey browns faster than sugar — watch closely near the end of baking.

recipes.name: Pecan Supremes
recipes.description: Oatmeal-based cookies loaded with both chopped pecans and chocolate chips.
ingredients: ¾ cup dark brown sugar, packed
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda, salt and oats; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl blend sugars with electric mixer at medium speed.
Add butter; mix to form a grainy paste; scrape down sides; add eggs and vanilla; beat until light and fluffy.
Add flour mixture, pecans and chocolate chips; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Drop dough by rounded tablespoons onto ungreased cookie sheets, 1½ inches apart.
Bake 20–22 minutes; immediately transfer cookies with a spatula to a cool flat surface.

recipes.name: Banana Nut Cookies
recipes.description: Moist banana cookies with walnuts and a double dose of chocolate chips — on top and mixed in.
ingredients: 1 cup light brown sugar, firmly packed
1 tsp crème de banana liqueur or pure banana extract
¾ cup mashed ripe banana (about 1 medium)
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda and salt; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl blend sugars with electric mixer at medium speed.
Add butter; mix to form a grainy paste, scraping down sides.
Add egg, liqueur and banana; beat at medium speed until smooth.
Add flour mixture, 1 cup of the chocolate chips and walnuts; blend at low speed until just combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoons onto ungreased cookie sheets, 2 inches apart.
Sprinkle remaining chocolate chips on top of each cookie (6–8 per cookie).
Bake 25–27 minutes or until edges begin to brown; transfer immediately to a cool surface.
tips: Use very ripe, brown-speckled bananas for the most flavor.

recipes.name: Nutty White Chunk Cookies
recipes.description: Light brown sugar cookies with chopped pecans and big chunks of white chocolate.
ingredients: 1 cup light brown sugar, firmly packed
1¼ cups (8 oz) white chocolate bar, coarsely chopped
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda and salt; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl blend sugars with electric mixer at medium speed.
Add butter; mix to form a grainy paste, scraping down sides; add eggs and vanilla; beat until light and fluffy.
Add flour mixture, pecans and white chocolate; blend at low speed until just combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoons onto ungreased cookie sheets, 2 inches apart.
Bake 20–22 minutes or until edges just begin to turn golden brown.
Transfer immediately to a cool flat surface with a spatula.

recipes.name: Pineapple Paradise Cookies
recipes.description: Tropical drop cookies made with crushed pineapple and a coconut topping.
ingredients: ¼ cup dark brown sugar, firmly packed
1 (8 oz) can crushed pineapple, well drained
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour and baking soda; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl blend sugars with electric mixer; add butter; mix to form a grainy paste, scraping down sides.
Add egg, vanilla, crushed pineapple and pineapple juice; beat on medium speed until smooth.
Add flour mixture; blend at low speed until just combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoons onto ungreased baking sheets, 2 inches apart.
Sprinkle lightly with shredded coconut.
Bake 22–24 minutes or until lightly brown at edges; transfer immediately to cool surface.
tips: Drain pineapple very well — excess moisture makes cookies spread too thin.

recipes.name: Krispies
recipes.description: Crispy chocolate chunk cookies with rice cereal mixed in for an irresistible crunch.
ingredients: ½ cup dark brown sugar, packed
1½ cups (8 oz) semisweet chocolate bar, coarsely chopped
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, salt and baking soda; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl blend sugars with electric mixer at medium speed.
Add butter; mix to form a grainy paste; scrape down sides; add egg and vanilla; beat until light and fluffy.
Add flour mixture, rice cereal and chocolate chunks; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoons onto ungreased cookie sheets, 2 inches apart.
Bake 22–24 minutes; immediately transfer cookies with a spatula to a cool flat surface.

recipes.name: Apple Oatmeal Cookies
recipes.description: Honey-sweetened oatmeal cookies with fresh apple, raisins, and a sprinkle of oats on top.
ingredients: 1 cup dark brown sugar, firmly packed
1 cup fresh apple, peeled and finely chopped
½ cup quick oats for topping (optional)
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, oats, salt, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves and lemon zest; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
Cream sugar and butter in a large bowl using electric mixer.
Add egg, applesauce and honey; beat at medium speed until smooth.
Add flour mixture, fresh apple and raisins; blend at low speed until just combined — dough will be soft. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoons onto ungreased baking sheets, 1½ inches apart; sprinkle with oats if desired.
Bake 23–25 minutes or until bottoms are golden.
tips: Dough will be quite soft — chill 15 minutes if too sticky to drop.

recipes.name: Black-and-Whites
recipes.description: Dark cocoa cookies packed with both semisweet and white chocolate chunks — a chocolate lover's contrast.
ingredients: 1 cup dark brown sugar, firmly packed
1 cup (5½ oz) semisweet chocolate bar, coarsely chopped
1 cup (5½ oz) white chocolate bar, coarsely chopped
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, cocoa, baking soda and salt; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
Blend sugars in a large bowl using electric mixer at medium speed.
Add butter; mix to form a grainy paste, scraping down sides; add eggs and vanilla; beat until smooth.
Add flour mixture and both chocolates; blend at low speed until just combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoons onto ungreased cookie sheets, 2 inches apart.
Bake 23–25 minutes; transfer immediately to cool flat surface.

recipes.name: Marbles
recipes.description: Swirled vanilla and chocolate cookies — melted chocolate is loosely folded in to create a marbled effect.
ingredients: ½ cup light brown sugar, firmly packed
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking powder and salt with wire whisk; set aside.
Combine sugars in a large bowl using electric mixer at medium speed; add butter; beat until grainy.
Add egg, sour cream and vanilla; beat at medium speed until light and fluffy; scrape bowl.
Add flour mixture; blend at low speed until just combined. Do not overmix.
Melt chocolate chips in a double boiler or microwave (stirring every 20 seconds); cool a few minutes.
Pour melted chocolate over cookie batter; lightly fold with a spoon — do not fully combine; batter should look swirled.
Drop by rounded tablespoons, 2 inches apart, onto ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake until set but not browned; transfer quickly to a cool surface.
tips: Stop folding while the chocolate is still visibly streaked — over-mixing ruins the marble effect.

recipes.name: Lemon Chocolate Chip Buttons
recipes.description: Small, delicate lemon and coriander cookies with miniature chocolate chips — bite-sized and bright.
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda and coriander; mix with wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl cream butter and sugar with electric mixer at medium speed to form a grainy paste.
Add eggs and lemon extract; beat well; scrape down sides of bowl.
Add flour mixture and chocolate chips; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Drop dough by teaspoonfuls (small!) onto ungreased baking sheets, 1½ inches apart.
Bake 14–15 minutes on center rack; do not brown.
Immediately transfer with a spatula to a cool surface.
tips: Use a teaspoon, not a tablespoon — these are meant to be small button-sized cookies.

recipes.name: Mandarin and Marmalade Cookies
recipes.description: Orange marmalade drop cookies with chopped mandarin orange pieces — fruity, soft, and fragrant.
ingredients: 1 (10 oz) can mandarin oranges, drained and chopped
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour and baking powder; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl blend butter and sugar with electric mixer to form a grainy paste.
Add egg and orange marmalade; beat at medium speed until smooth.
Add flour mixture and chopped oranges; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoonfuls onto ungreased baking sheets, 1½ inches apart.
Bake 24–25 minutes or until bottoms begin to brown.
Transfer with a spatula to a cool flat surface.
tips: Drain mandarin oranges thoroughly to avoid soggy cookies.

recipes.name: Orange Chocolate Chunk Cookies
recipes.description: Citrus-kissed cookies with fresh orange peel and rough-chopped semisweet chocolate.
ingredients: 1 tsp grated orange peel (from one medium orange)
½ cup light brown sugar, packed
1½ cups (8 oz) semisweet chocolate bar, coarsely chopped
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda, salt and orange peel; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl blend sugars with electric mixer at medium speed; add butter; beat to form a grainy paste.
Add eggs and orange extract; beat at medium speed until light and fluffy.
Add flour mixture and chopped chocolate; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoons onto ungreased cookie sheets, 1½ inches apart.
Bake 22–24 minutes until slightly brown along edges; transfer immediately to a cool surface.
tips: Grate only the orange-colored outer zest; avoid the bitter white pith.

recipes.name: Eggnog Cookies
recipes.description: Soft holiday cookies made with real eggnog and finished with a nutmeg sprinkle.
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking powder, cinnamon and nutmeg; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl cream sugar and butter with electric mixer to form a grainy paste.
Add eggnog, vanilla and egg yolks; beat at medium speed until smooth.
Add flour mixture; beat at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded teaspoonfuls onto ungreased baking sheets, 1 inch apart.
Sprinkle lightly with ground nutmeg.
Bake 23–25 minutes or until bottoms turn light brown.
Transfer to cool flat surface immediately.
tips: These are a must for the holiday cookie tray.

recipes.name: Fruitcake Cookies
recipes.description: Fruit-and-nut packed oatmeal cookies with brandy, molasses, and candied cherries — fruitcake made easy.
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking powder and oats; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl cream butter and sugar with electric mixer at medium speed; mix to form a grainy paste.
Add molasses, brandy, almond extract and vanilla; add eggs; beat until smooth.
Add flour mixture, raisins, pecans, almonds and cherries; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoonfuls onto ungreased baking sheets, 1½ inches apart.
Bake 22–24 minutes or until cookies are set; let set on pan 2–3 minutes.
Transfer to cool flat surface; top each cookie with a candied cherry half.
tips: Topping each cookie with a cherry half makes them look festive.

recipes.name: Chocolate Chip Raisin Cookies
recipes.description: The classic combo of plump raisins and chocolate chips in a soft, buttery cookie.
ingredients: ½ cup light brown sugar, firmly packed
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour and baking powder; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
Blend sugars in a large bowl using electric mixer at medium speed.
Add butter; mix until grainy, scraping down sides of bowl.
Add eggs and vanilla; mix at medium speed until smooth.
Add flour mixture, raisins and chocolate chips; blend at low speed until just combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoons onto ungreased baking sheets, 1½ inches apart.
Bake 22–24 minutes; transfer cookies immediately to a cool flat surface.

recipes.name: Apricot Nectar Cookies
recipes.description: Fruity drop cookies made with apricot nectar, apricot preserves, and chopped dried apricots.
ingredients: ¼ cup dark brown sugar, packed
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour and baking soda; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl blend sugars with electric mixer at medium speed.
Add butter; mix to form a grainy paste; scrape down sides.
Add egg, apricot nectar and apricot preserves; beat at medium speed until smooth.
Add flour mixture and chopped apricots; blend on low just until combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoonfuls onto ungreased baking sheets, 2 inches apart.
Bake 22–24 minutes or until cookies just begin to brown at bottom edges.
Let cookies cool on baking sheet 5 minutes before transferring to a cool flat surface.
tips: Letting cookies rest 5 minutes on the hot pan helps them set without overbaking.

recipes.name: Cholesterol-Free Chocolate Chip Cookies
recipes.description: Egg-yolk-free, margarine-based chocolate chip cookies sweetened with honey — lighter but still delicious.
ingredients: ¾ cup dark brown sugar, packed
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda and salt; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl blend sugars with electric mixer; add margarine; mix to form a grainy paste.
In a small bowl beat egg whites until fluffy.
Add egg whites, honey and vanilla to sugar mixture; beat until smooth; scrape down sides.
Add flour mixture and chocolate chips; blend on low just until combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheets, 1¾ inches apart.
Bake 18–20 minutes until lightly browned; immediately transfer with spatula to a cool flat surface.
tips: Beat egg whites to soft peaks for the lightest texture.

recipes.name: Peanut Butter Oatmeal Ranch Cookies
recipes.description: Hearty cookies with whole wheat flour, oats, peanut butter, honey, raisins, and sunflower seeds.
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flours, baking powder and oats; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl beat sugar and butter with electric mixer at medium speed to form a grainy paste.
Add peanut butter, honey, eggs and vanilla; blend together; scrape down sides of bowl.
Add flour mixture, raisins and sunflower seeds; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoonfuls onto ungreased baking sheets, 2 inches apart.
Bake 23–25 minutes until bottoms turn golden brown; immediately transfer with spatula to cool flat surface.

recipes.name: Cashew and Coconut Cookies
recipes.description: Tropical-inspired cookies with chopped cashews, shredded coconut, dates, and a coconut topping.
ingredients: ¼ cup light brown sugar, packed
1 cup (4 oz) chopped raw cashews, unsalted
¼ cup sweetened shredded coconut, reserved for topping
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda and salt; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
In a medium bowl combine sugars with electric mixer at medium speed.
Add butter; mix to form a grainy paste; add eggs and vanilla; beat until smooth.
Add flour mixture, coconut, cashews and dates; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoonfuls onto ungreased baking sheets, 2 inches apart.
Sprinkle tops with reserved coconut.
Bake 23–25 minutes or until bottoms turn golden brown; transfer to cool flat surface.
tips: The coconut topping toasts beautifully and adds visual appeal.

recipes.name: Lacy Oatmeal Cookies
recipes.description: Crispy, paper-thin oatmeal wafers that spread into delicate lace — cool and peel right off the foil.
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F; cover baking sheets with foil, then coat with nonstick vegetable spray.
In a medium bowl combine oats, flour, salt and baking powder; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl combine sugar and butter with electric mixer at medium speed to form a grainy paste.
Add egg and vanilla; beat until smooth; add flour mixture; blend just until combined.
Drop dough by teaspoonfuls onto prepared baking sheets, 2½ inches apart (they spread a lot).
Bake 10–12 minutes or until edges begin to turn golden brown.
Cool on the pan, then peel off cookies with your fingers.
Respray baking sheets between batches.
tips: These need to cool completely before peeling or they will tear.
Use foil — parchment tears when peeling these thin cookies.

recipes.name: Cocomia Cookies
recipes.description: Coconut macadamia cookies — shredded unsweetened coconut and whole macadamia nuts in every bite.
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda and salt; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl blend sugars with electric mixer at medium speed.
Add butter; mix to form a grainy paste; scrape down sides; add eggs and vanilla; beat until light and fluffy.
Add flour mixture, coconut and macadamia nuts; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Drop by rounded tablespoons onto ungreased cookie sheets, 2 inches apart.
Bake 22–24 minutes; immediately transfer cookies with spatula to a cool flat surface.

recipes.name: Applesauce Oaties
recipes.description: Quick-baked oatmeal cookies with applesauce, chocolate chips, raisins, and walnuts.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
In a medium bowl combine oats, flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, cinnamon and nutmeg; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl combine sugars with electric mixer at medium speed; add butter; beat to form a grainy paste.
Add egg and applesauce; blend until smooth.
Add flour mixture, chocolate chips, raisins and walnuts; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Drop dough by tablespoonfuls onto lightly greased baking sheets, 2 inches apart.
Bake 12–14 minutes or until light brown; immediately transfer with spatula to a cool flat surface.
tips: These bake at 375°F — hotter than most Mrs. Fields cookies — so watch them closely.

recipes.name: Bizcochitos
recipes.description: Traditional New Mexican cookies with aniseed and brandy, pressed into cinnamon-sugar before baking.
ingredients: ¾ cup light brown sugar, firmly packed
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
Whisk together flour, baking soda, salt and aniseed in a bowl; set aside.
Blend sugars in a medium bowl using electric mixer at medium speed.
Add butter; mix until grainy, scraping down sides; add eggs and brandy; beat until light and fluffy.
Add flour mixture; mix at low speed until just combined. Do not overmix.
Mix together the cinnamon-sugar topping in a small bowl.
Roll rounded tablespoons of dough into 1-inch diameter balls; flatten slightly with the bottom of a glass.
Press tops into the cinnamon-sugar mixture; place on ungreased cookie sheets, 1½ inches apart.
Bake 22–24 minutes until slightly brown along edges; transfer immediately with a spatula.
tips: Aniseed gives these their distinctive flavor — don't substitute anise extract.

recipes.name: Molasses Raisin Cookies
recipes.description: Spiced molasses cookies shaped into a log, chilled, and sliced — drizzled with a simple sugar icing.
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, ginger and allspice; mix well with wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl beat sugar and butter with electric mixer until mixture forms a grainy paste; scrape sides.
Add molasses and egg; beat until light and fluffy.
Add flour mixture and raisins; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Divide dough in half; shape each half into a roll 1½ inches in diameter.
Wrap rolls in waxed paper; refrigerate until firm, about 2 hours.
Slice cookies ¼ inch thick; place on ungreased cookie sheets, 1½ inches apart.
Bake 25–27 minutes until cookies are set; transfer immediately to a cool surface.
Prepare icing: blend confectioners' sugar and milk in a small bowl until smooth; drizzle over cooled cookies.
tips: Refrigerated dough logs can be frozen for up to 1 month.
Slice with a sharp knife for clean edges.

recipes.name: Mapo Tofu
recipes.description: Silky tofu in a spicy, numbing Sichuan sauce with ground pork - a classic grandmother's dish.
instructions: Cube tofu and set aside
Toast Sichuan peppercorns in a dry pan, crush lightly
Heat oil, stir-fry pork until cooked
Add doubanjiang and garlic, fry until fragrant
Add stock and soy sauce, bring to simmer
Gently add tofu cubes, simmer 10 minutes
Mix cornstarch with water, add to thicken
Drizzle sesame oil, garnish with green onions
tips: Use silken tofu for authentic texture
Sichuan peppercorns create the numbing sensation
Don't stir too aggressively to keep tofu intact
This dish improves with time - make ahead if possible

recipes.name: Lion's Head Meatballs
recipes.description: Tender pork meatballs with water chestnuts, served in a silky sauce - named for their appearance.
instructions: Mix pork, water chestnuts, green onions, soy sauce, rice wine, sesame oil, and cornstarch
Form into 8-12 large meatballs
Heat oil in pan, brown meatballs on all sides
Add stock and oyster sauce
Layer napa cabbage on top of meatballs
Cover and simmer 20 minutes until cooked through
Serve in the sauce
tips: Large meatballs stay juicier than small ones
Water chestnuts add authentic texture
Don't overmix the meat mixture
Napa cabbage absorbs the delicious sauce

substitutions.Oyster sauce: Soy sauce + a touch of sugar

recipes.name: Kung Pao Chicken
recipes.description: Tender chicken with cashews in a spicy-sweet Sichuan sauce - quick and satisfying.
instructions: Heat oil in wok or large pan until smoking
Add dried chilies, remove when fragrant
Add chicken, stir-fry until cooked through
Add garlic and ginger, stir 30 seconds
Add soy sauce, vinegar, and sugar
Toss in cashews, drizzle sesame oil
Stir to combine, serve immediately
tips: High heat is essential for proper wok cooking
Don't overcook the chicken - cube evenly for uniform cooking
Cashews add richness and contrast
Serve over rice to soak up the sauce

recipes.name: Kimchi Jjigae
recipes.description: Spicy kimchi stew with tofu and pork - a warming Korean comfort dish.
instructions: Heat oil, fry pork until partially cooked
Add kimchi, fry 2-3 minutes
Add gochugaru, stir to combine
Add stock and bring to boil
Add gochujang, garlic, sugar, and soy sauce
Add tofu cubes, simmer 15 minutes
Top with green onion, serve hot with rice
tips: Kimchi should be fermented at least 3-5 days
The stew tastes better the next day
Serve with a fresh, crispy side dish for balance
Adjust spice level to your preference
recipes.cookbook: Cook Korean: A Comic Book with Recipes

recipes.name: Bulgogi
recipes.description: Marinated beef grilled Korean-style - sweet, savory, and incredibly tender.
ingredients: 1.5 lbs thinly sliced beef (ribeye or sirloin)
instructions: Combine soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, garlic, vinegar, ginger, and pear
Marinate beef at least 30 minutes (overnight is better)
Heat a cast iron skillet or grill until very hot
Cook beef in batches, 2-3 minutes per side
Garnish with sesame seeds and green onions
Serve with rice and lettuce wraps
tips: Partially freeze beef for easier slicing
Pear adds natural enzymes for tenderness
High heat creates a nice char
Wrap in lettuce with ssamjang sauce
recipes.cookbook: Cook Korean: A Comic Book with Recipes

recipes.name: Japchae
recipes.description: Stir-fried sweet potato noodles with vegetables - a festive Korean side dish.
instructions: Cook noodles according to package, drain and mix with 1 tbsp sesame oil
Stir-fry beef in hot oil, set aside
Stir-fry vegetables separately, season lightly with salt
Blanch spinach, squeeze dry, mix with garlic and sesame oil
Combine noodles with soy sauce, sugar, and 1 tbsp sesame oil
Mix all components together gently
Garnish with sesame seeds and serve at room temperature
tips: Each ingredient is cooked separately for best flavor
Don't overcook - vegetables should have slight crunch
Serve at room temperature or slightly warm
Great for meal prep

substitutions.Beef: Shrimp or more vegetables for vegetarian

recipes.cookbook: Cook Korean: A Comic Book with Recipes

recipes.name: Miso Ramen
recipes.description: Rich miso-flavored ramen with homemade broth - a warming Japanese classic.
instructions: Simmer stock with ginger and garlic for 20 minutes
Strain broth, return to pot
Whisk miso with small amount of broth, add back to pot
Add soy sauce and mirin, taste and adjust
Cook ramen noodles separately according to package
Divide noodles between bowls
Pour hot broth over noodles
Top with soft-boiled egg, mushrooms, green onions, nori, and sprouts
tips: Make miso broth base in advance for convenience
Soft-boil eggs by simmering 6-7 minutes in water
Don't add miso directly to hot broth - it kills beneficial enzymes
Customize toppings based on preference

recipes.name: Chicken Katsu
recipes.description: Crispy breaded chicken cutlet served with tangy tonkatsu sauce - a beloved Japanese comfort food.
ingredients: 1/2 cup tonkatsu sauce (or Worcestershire + ketchup + soy)
instructions: Pound chicken breasts to even thickness
Set up breading station: flour, beaten egg, panko
Coat chicken in flour, shaking off excess
Dip in egg, then coat thoroughly with panko
Heat oil to 350°F (175°C)
Fry chicken 4-5 minutes per side until golden
Drain on paper towels
Serve with tonkatsu sauce, mayo, and fresh cabbage
tips: Pound evenly for uniform cooking
Use panko for extra crispiness
Temperature control prevents greasy coating
Serve immediately while still crispy

recipes.name: Sushi Rice Balls
recipes.description: Vinegared sushi rice shaped into perfect balls - foundation for many Japanese dishes.
instructions: Rinse rice 3-4 times until water runs clear
Cook rice with 2.5 cups water
Heat vinegar, sugar, salt, and mirin until dissolved
Transfer hot rice to a bowl
Pour vinegar mixture over rice, fold gently
Cool rice to room temperature
Wet hands with water-vinegar mixture
Form rice into balls, pressing gently but firmly
tips: Don't wash rice too much - removes starch needed for stickiness
Cool rice completely before shaping
Wet hands between each ball
Rice balls stay fresh for several hours

recipes.name: Okonomiyaki
recipes.description: Japanese savory pancakes with cabbage and protein - a fun, customizable street food.
instructions: Mix flour, water, and egg to make batter
Layer batter, cabbage, and pork in a pan
Cook on medium heat 8-10 minutes until golden
Flip carefully, cook another 8-10 minutes
Spread okonomiyaki sauce and mayo on top
Sprinkle with bonito flakes and aonori
Top with green onions, serve hot
tips: Make a well in the center for even cooking
Don't flip too early - wait for golden crust
Bonito flakes wave from heat residual - very fun!
Customize with shrimp, squid, or cheese

substitutions.Pork belly: Shrimp, squid, mushrooms, or skip for vegetarian

recipes.name: Cinnamon Sugar Butter Cookies
recipes.description: Buttery drop cookies rolled in cinnamon-sugar before baking — crisp edges, tender centers.
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a small bowl combine 3 tbsp sugar and cinnamon for topping; set aside.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda and salt; mix well with a wire whisk and set aside.
In a large bowl blend both sugars with an electric mixer at medium speed; add butter and mix to form a grainy paste; scrape sides of bowl.
Add eggs and vanilla; beat at medium speed until light and fluffy.
Add the flour mixture; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Shape dough into 1-inch balls; roll each ball in the cinnamon-sugar topping.
Place on ungreased cookie sheets, 2 inches apart.
Bake 18–20 minutes until set; transfer immediately to a cool flat surface.
tips: Use a cookie scoop for uniform ball size.
Roll each ball thoroughly in the topping — the cinnamon-sugar crust is what makes these special.

recipes.name: Gingersnaps
recipes.description: Spicy, crisp cookies with both ground and crystallized ginger — a peppery kick from black pepper.
ingredients: 1½ cups dark brown sugar, firmly packed
instructions: In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda, salt, ground ginger, crystallized ginger, allspice and pepper; mix well with a wire whisk and set aside.
In a large bowl mix sugar and butter with an electric mixer at medium speed; scrape down sides of bowl.
Add egg and molasses; beat at medium speed until light and fluffy.
Add the flour mixture; mix at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Chill the dough in the refrigerator for 1 hour — it will be less sticky and easier to handle.
Preheat oven to 300°F.
Form dough into 1-inch diameter balls; place on ungreased cookie sheets, 1½ inches apart.
Bake 24–25 minutes until set.
Use a spatula to immediately transfer cookies to a cool, flat surface.
tips: The black pepper is intentional — it brightens the spice profile.
Chilling the dough is essential; skip it and the cookies will spread too much.

recipes.name: Macadamia Nut Coconut Crisps
recipes.description: Thin, lacy crisps made by cooking butter, corn syrup and sugar, then stirring in macadamias, coconut and chocolate chips.
ingredients: 1 cup (4 oz) raw macadamia nuts, coarsely chopped
1½ cups dark brown sugar, firmly packed
½ cup (2 oz) miniature semisweet chocolate chips
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Whisk together flour, macadamia nuts and coconut in a medium bowl; set aside.
Heat butter, corn syrup and brown sugar in a 2-quart saucepan until boiling, stirring occasionally.
Remove saucepan from heat; stir in vanilla.
Add flour mixture and chocolate chips; mix until all ingredients are equally distributed.
Drop by half-teaspoonfuls onto well-greased cookie sheets, 2 inches apart.
Bake 8–10 minutes or until mixture spreads, bubbles and lightly browns.
Cool cookies 1 minute on pan, then immediately transfer to a cool flat surface with a metal spatula.
Cookies will remain soft until completely cooled; they crisp as they cool.
tips: These spread a lot — leave plenty of space between drops.
Gently fold the dry mixture into the hot liquid a little at a time, stirring after each addition.

recipes.name: Maple Pecan Butter Balls
recipes.description: Tender maple-flavored butter balls loaded with finely ground pecans — delicate and nutty.
ingredients: ¾ cup (3 oz) pecans, finely ground
instructions: In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda, cinnamon and ground pecans; mix well with a wire whisk and set aside.
In a medium bowl cream butter and sugar with an electric mixer at medium speed until mixture forms a grainy paste.
Add maple syrup and egg; beat until slightly thickened.
Add the flour mixture; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Place dough in a plastic bag and refrigerate until firm, about 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 300°F.
Remove dough from refrigerator; shape into 1-inch balls.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet, 1 inch apart.
Bake 17–18 minutes or until cookie bottoms are golden brown; transfer immediately to a cool surface.
tips: For extra flavor, sauté pecans in 1 tablespoon butter until lightly browned before grinding.
Finely ground pecans give the cookies a sandy, melt-in-your-mouth texture.

recipes.name: Choconut Macaroons
recipes.description: Light coconut macaroons with almond paste and mini chocolate chips — crisp outside, chewy inside.
ingredients: ½ cup (2 oz) miniature semisweet chocolate chips
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F.
Combine almond paste and sugar in a medium bowl; using your fingers, work paste into sugar completely.
Add coconut and chocolate chips; stir to combine.
In a clean medium bowl with absolutely clean beaters, beat egg whites until fluffy.
Add cream of tartar; beat on high until stiff peaks form.
Add half of beaten egg whites to coconut mixture; stir to lighten.
Fold in remaining whites gently with a spatula, being careful not to deflate.
Drop by rounded teaspoons onto lightly greased cookie sheets.
Bake 20 minutes until tops are lightly browned; cool 1 minute before transferring.
tips: Any trace of fat on bowl or beaters will prevent whites from whipping to stiff peaks.
Fold the second half of the egg whites gently — lift from the bottom up over the top.

recipes.name: Cinnamon Maple Rings
recipes.description: Flaky maple pastry rolled with cinnamon-sugar filling, chilled twice, sliced into delicate spiral rings.
ingredients: 1 cup salted butter, chilled and sliced into 8 pieces
¾ cup pure maple syrup, chilled
instructions: Combine flour and sugar in a medium bowl using an electric mixer at medium speed.
Add chilled butter; mix until dough forms small, pea-sized pellets.
Add chilled maple syrup and 2 tablespoons ice water; mix on low speed until dough forms a ball. Do not overmix.
Separate dough into 2 balls; flatten into disks and wrap tightly in plastic wrap; refrigerate 2 hours.
Combine filling sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl.
Preheat oven to 325°F.
On a floured surface, roll one disk into a rectangle roughly 10 inches wide, 15 inches long, and ¼ inch thick.
Sprinkle with half the cinnamon-sugar filling; starting from the shorter side, roll dough up tightly into a cylinder; dampen edge with water and seal.
Repeat with remaining dough; wrap each roll in plastic wrap and refrigerate 1 hour.
Slice each roll ¼ inch thick with a sharp thin knife; place on ungreased baking sheets, 1 inch apart.
Brush tops lightly with maple syrup.
Bake 16–17 minutes or until light golden brown; transfer immediately to a cool flat surface.
tips: Chilling the dough twice — as disks, then as logs — is the key to clean, neat slices.
Brush with maple syrup just before sliding into the oven for a glossy, caramelized top.

recipes.name: Gingerbread Men
recipes.description: Classic soft gingerbread men with cinnamon, ginger and cloves — decorated with piped icing and raisin buttons.
ingredients: ¾ cup dark brown sugar, firmly packed
instructions: Whisk together flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, ginger and cloves in a medium bowl.
In a large bowl cream butter and sugar with an electric mixer; scrape bowl; add egg and molasses; beat at medium speed until smooth.
Add flour mixture; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Divide dough into 2 balls; flatten each into a disk; wrap tightly in plastic; refrigerate 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 325°F.
On a floured surface with a floured rolling pin, roll dough to ¼-inch thickness.
Cut out gingerbread men with floured cookie cutters; gather scraps and reroll until all dough is used.
Place on ungreased baking sheets ½ inch apart; optionally press raisins for eyes, mouths and buttons.
Bake 9–11 minutes, being careful not to brown; transfer to a cool flat surface.
For icing: whisk sugar and milk until smooth and liquid; pipe onto cooled cookies as desired.
tips: Roll out evenly to ¼ inch — uneven thickness leads to unevenly baked cookies.
The icing should be thin enough to pipe but not runny; add milk a few drops at a time.

recipes.name: Christmas Sugar Cookies
recipes.description: Simple rolled sugar cookies cut into holiday shapes and decorated with colored sugars or sprinkles.
ingredients: Colored sugars or sprinkles for decorating
instructions: Combine flour and salt in a medium bowl with a wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl cream butter and sugar with an electric mixer at medium speed; add egg and vanilla; beat until well mixed.
Scrape bowl; add flour mixture; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Gather dough into a ball; flatten into a disk; wrap tightly in plastic; refrigerate 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 325°F.
On a floured surface, roll dough to ¼-inch thickness; cut into desired shapes with floured cookie cutters.
Place on ungreased cookie sheets; decorate with colored sugars or sprinkles.
Bake 13–15 minutes, being careful not to brown; transfer immediately to a cool flat surface.
tips: Keep the dough cold — warm dough is hard to cut cleanly.
Reroll scraps only once; overworked dough makes tough cookies.

recipes.name: Brown Buttercrunch Cookies
recipes.description: Ultra-thin lace cookies made on the stovetop, rolled around a spoon handle while hot, then dipped in chocolate glaze.
ingredients: ¾ cup dark brown sugar, packed
1 cup old-fashioned oats (not quick or instant)
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F; line cookie sheets with parchment paper.
In a medium saucepan melt butter, corn syrup and brown sugar over moderate heat, stirring until sugar dissolves.
Increase heat to high; when mixture boils, remove from heat and stir in oats, flour and vanilla.
Bake one pan at a time — drop half-teaspoonfuls 3 inches apart onto parchment-lined sheets.
Bake 8 minutes or until mixture spreads, bubbles and begins to brown.
Let cool 1–2 minutes, then roll each warm cookie around a pencil or wooden spoon handle to form a tube.
If cookies become too brittle, return to oven for about 30 seconds to soften.
For the glaze: heat cream in a small saucepan until scalded; remove from heat; stir in chocolate chips and corn syrup; cover and let stand 15 minutes.
Stir glaze gently with a whisk until smooth; dip all or half of each cooled cookie tube into glaze; return to parchment; allow to set.
tips: Work fast — these harden quickly after coming out of the oven.
Don't create bubbles when stirring the chocolate glaze; stir slowly and gently.

recipes.name: Sweetie Pies
recipes.description: Intensely chocolatey cookies made with melted chocolate and three types of chips — semisweet, white and milk chocolate.
ingredients: ¾ cup (4 oz) semisweet chocolate chips
½ cup (3 oz) white chocolate chips
¼ cup (1.5 oz) milk chocolate chips
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F; line cookie sheets with waxed paper.
In a double boiler melt the unsweetened chocolate and first batch of semisweet chips, stirring frequently until creamy and smooth.
Pour melted chocolate into a large bowl; add butter; beat with electric mixer at medium speed until thoroughly combined.
Add sugar, eggs and vanilla; beat at medium speed until well blended; scrape sides of bowl.
Add flour and all three types of chocolate chips; mix at low speed just until combined.
Roll a heaping tablespoon of dough into a ball about 1½ inches in diameter; place 2 inches apart on waxed-paper-lined pans.
With the palm of your hand, flatten each ball to ½-inch thickness.
Bake 10–12 minutes; transfer to a cool flat surface.
tips: Using three kinds of chips creates layers of chocolate flavor in every bite.
Don't overbake — these should look slightly underdone when they come out of the oven.

recipes.name: Party Time Cookies
recipes.description: Buttery cookies with almond extract, semisweet chocolate chips and slivered almonds — simple and festive.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Cream butter and sugar together in a medium bowl using an electric mixer at medium speed.
Add vanilla and almond extracts; beat well; scrape bowl.
Add flour, chocolate chips and almonds; blend at low speed until just combined. Do not overmix.
Shape rounded tablespoonfuls into 1½-inch balls; place on ungreased baking sheets, 2 inches apart.
Press balls with the palm of your hand or the bottom of a glass into ½-inch-thick rounds.
Bake 15–17 minutes or until cookies just begin to brown.
Transfer cookies to a cool flat surface.
tips: The almond extract is the flavor that makes these distinctive — don't skip it.
Press gently when flattening so the cookies don't crumble.

recipes.name: Snowy White Chocolate Crescents
recipes.description: Rich chocolate crescent cookies with a dry, crumbly dough shaped into logs, then bent and rolled in confectioners' sugar while warm.
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F.
Combine flour and cocoa in a small bowl; mix well with a wire whisk and set aside.
In a medium bowl cream butter and sugar with an electric mixer at medium speed; add vanilla and egg; beat until light and smooth; scrape sides of bowl.
Add flour-cocoa mixture; blend at low speed until fully incorporated. The dough will be dry and crumbly.
Shape a level tablespoonful of dough into a 3½-inch log; slightly bend the log to form a crescent shape.
Place crescents on ungreased baking sheets, 1 inch apart.
Bake 15–17 minutes or until the outside is hard but the center remains slightly soft.
Cool on pan 2–3 minutes; transfer to a flat surface.
While still warm, roll each cookie in confectioners' sugar until well coated.
tips: Roll in powdered sugar while the cookies are still warm so it adheres.
If the dough is too crumbly to shape, press it firmly in your hands — body heat helps it come together.

recipes.name: Apple Cobbler Cookies
recipes.description: Apple butter and fresh apple cookies rolled in an oat-cinnamon crumb coating — like a portable apple cobbler.
ingredients: ½ cup light brown sugar, firmly packed
1 cup tart apple, peeled and chopped
1¼ cups light brown sugar, firmly packed (crumb coating)
1½ cups quick oats, not instant (crumb coating)
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking powder and cinnamon; mix well with a wire whisk; set aside.
Combine sugars in a large bowl; add butter; mix with electric mixer at medium speed; scrape bowl.
Add eggs and vanilla; blend until smooth; thoroughly incorporate apple juice and apple butter.
Add flour mixture, chopped apple, raisins and pecans; blend at low speed until just combined. Do not overmix.
For the crumb coating: combine brown sugar, oats and cinnamon in a medium bowl; add melted butter; stir until dry ingredients are well moistened.
Roll dough into 1-inch-diameter balls; roll each ball in the crumb mixture until well coated, pressing to make it stick.
Place on ungreased cookie sheets, 2 inches apart.
Bake 24–26 minutes or until cookie is firm to the touch and crumb topping begins to brown; transfer to a cool flat surface.
tips: Press the crumb coating firmly into the dough ball to make it stick.
Use a firm tart apple like Granny Smith for the best texture and flavor.

recipes.name: Russian Tea Cakes
recipes.description: Buttery thumbprint cookies filled with fruit preserves or chopped walnuts, then dusted with confectioners' sugar.
ingredients: ½ cup fruit preserves or ½ cup (2 oz) chopped walnuts (filling)
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F.
In a large bowl cream butter and sugar using an electric mixer; add vanilla; scrape bowl as needed.
Blend in flour and salt; mix until thoroughly combined.
Roll tablespoonfuls of dough into 1-inch balls; place on lightly greased cookie sheets about 1 inch apart.
Press down the center of each ball with a spoon to form a depression.
Fill each depression with a teaspoonful of preserves or chopped walnuts.
Bake 15–20 minutes or until golden brown; transfer immediately to a cool flat surface.
When completely cool, dust lightly with confectioners' sugar.
tips: Make the depression deep enough to hold the filling without it spilling during baking.
Jam fillings will bubble and set as the cookies cool — let them cool fully before handling.

recipes.name: Brown Sugar Shortbread
recipes.description: Brown sugar shortbread logs dipped in dark chocolate and rolled in chopped pecans.
ingredients: ¾ cup light brown sugar, packed
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F.
In a large bowl cream butter and sugar with an electric mixer at medium speed; scrape down sides.
Add vanilla and flour; blend thoroughly at low speed.
Shape level tablespoonfuls of dough into 1-inch balls, then form into 2-inch logs.
Place on ungreased baking sheets, 2 inches apart.
Bake 17–19 minutes or until cookies spread and turn light golden brown; transfer to a cool flat surface.
For the topping: melt butter and chocolate chips in a double boiler or microwave, stirring every 30 seconds until smooth.
Dip the top of each cooled cookie into melted chocolate, then into chopped pecans.
Place on waxed paper and refrigerate to set.
tips: Keep bowls of chocolate and pecans close together for a quick, smooth assembly line dip.
Refrigerating after dipping gives a clean, firm chocolate shell.

recipes.name: Chocolate Cream-Filled Hearts
recipes.description: Delicate butter cookie hearts sandwiched with silky ganache filling — dusted with confectioners' sugar.
instructions: Cream butter in a medium bowl with electric mixer at medium speed; add confectioners' sugar; beat until smooth; add vanilla; mix until creamy.
Scrape bowl; add flour; mix at low speed until thoroughly combined.
Gather dough into 2 balls; flatten to disks; wrap tightly in plastic; refrigerate 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 325°F.
Using a floured rolling pin, roll dough on a floured board to ¼-inch thickness; cut out 2-inch hearts.
Place on ungreased cookie sheets ½ inch apart; bake 16–18 minutes until firm; transfer to a cool surface.
For the filling: scald cream in a small saucepan; remove from heat; stir in chocolate chips; cover 15 minutes; stir until smooth; cool to room temperature.
Spread 1 teaspoonful of chocolate filling on the bottom of half the cookies; top with another cookie bottom-side down to form a sandwich.
Sift confectioners' sugar over finished cookies if desired.
tips: The chocolate filling sets up as it cools — make it first and let it cool while you bake.
Spread the filling on the flat (bottom) side of each heart for a neater look.

recipes.name: Chocolate Sandwich Cookies
recipes.description: Homemade chocolate wafer cookies sandwiched with a classic vanilla cream filling — like a from-scratch Oreo.
instructions: Cream butter in a medium bowl with electric mixer at medium speed; add confectioners' sugar; beat until smooth; add vanilla; beat until light and fluffy.
In a separate bowl combine cocoa, cornstarch and flour; mix well with a wire whisk.
Add cocoa mixture to the wet ingredients; mix at low speed until thoroughly combined.
Gather dough into a disk; wrap tightly in plastic; refrigerate 1½ hours.
Preheat oven to 325°F.
Roll dough on a floured board to ¼-inch thickness; cut shapes with cookie cutters; place on ungreased sheets 1 inch apart.
Bake 16–18 minutes until firm; transfer to a cool surface.
For the filling: cream butter; add sugar, vanilla and cream; beat until smooth.
Spread ½ teaspoon of cream filling on the bottom side of half the cookies; top with remaining cookies.
tips: Cornstarch in the dough gives these a delicate, snap-like texture.
Fill cookies the same day for softest texture, or 1–2 days ahead for a firmer, classic sandwich-cookie bite.

recipes.name: Fruit-Filled Jewels
recipes.description: Buttery round cookies with a pocket of your favorite fruit jam, sealed with fork tines — simple but charming.
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F.
In a medium bowl cream butter with an electric mixer at medium speed; add sugar; beat until smooth.
Add egg yolks and vanilla; beat at medium speed until light and fluffy.
Add flour; blend at low speed until thoroughly combined.
Gather dough into a disk; wrap in plastic; refrigerate 1 hour.
Using a floured rolling pin, roll dough to ¼-inch thickness; cut circles with a 2-inch cookie cutter.
Place circles on ungreased cookie sheets 1 inch apart.
Drop ½ teaspoon of jam in the center of each circle; top with another circle; seal edges with the tines of a fork.
Bake 15–17 minutes or until edges begin to brown.
tips: Use a thick jam — runny preserves will leak out when sealed.
Fork-sealing prevents the filling from bubbling out; press firmly all the way around.

recipes.name: Chocolate Dreams
recipes.description: Rolled chocolate cookie rounds sandwiched with a rich ganache filling — sprinkled with white sugar.
ingredients: ¾ cup light brown sugar, firmly packed
instructions: In a medium bowl cream butter with electric mixer at medium speed; add both sugars; beat until smooth.
Add egg yolks and vanilla; beat at medium speed until light and fluffy; scrape bowl.
Add flour; blend at low speed until thoroughly combined.
Gather dough into a disk; wrap in plastic; refrigerate 1 hour.
For the filling: scald cream in a small saucepan over medium heat; add chocolate chips; stir until melted; remove from heat and cool to room temperature.
Preheat oven to 325°F.
Roll dough to ¼-inch thickness on a floured board; cut circles with a 2-inch cookie cutter; place on ungreased sheets 1 inch apart.
Drop 1 teaspoon of chocolate filling in center of each circle; top with another circle; seal edges completely with a fork.
Bake 15–16 minutes or until golden brown; transfer to a cool surface; sprinkle with white sugar while still warm.
tips: Let the ganache filling cool until it thickens to a spreadable consistency before filling the cookies.
Seal the edges firmly with a fork so filling stays inside during baking.

recipes.name: Custard-Filled Cookies
recipes.description: Vanilla thumbprint cookies filled with a homemade cooked custard — silky, elegant, and impressive.
ingredients: 1 vanilla bean or 1 tsp pure vanilla extract (custard)
Ground cinnamon, confectioners' sugar, or cocoa powder (for dusting)
instructions: In a medium saucepan over medium heat, heat condensed milk with vanilla until small bubbles form.
Whisk egg yolks in a bowl; slowly add ½ cup of the hot milk to the yolks while stirring (tempering).
Add the tempered yolks back into the saucepan; cook, stirring constantly, 5 minutes until custard coats the back of a spoon. Do not boil.
Strain custard through a sieve; refrigerate until thoroughly chilled.
Preheat oven to 325°F.
Mix butter and sugar in a medium bowl with electric mixer; add egg and cream; mix until thoroughly blended; scrape bowl.
Add flour; blend at low speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Shape dough into 1-inch balls; place on ungreased sheets 1 inch apart; form a small depression in the center of each with your thumb.
Bake 15–17 minutes or until bottoms begin to brown; transfer to a cool surface.
When cookies reach room temperature, spoon or pipe 1½ teaspoons of chilled custard into each depression; dust with cinnamon, powdered sugar or cocoa.
tips: Tempering the egg yolks prevents scrambling — always add hot liquid to yolks slowly, never the reverse.
The custard must be fully chilled before filling cookies or it will melt and run.

recipes.name: Linzer Cookies
recipes.description: Almond-flavored butter cookies with indented centers filled with raspberry jam and lemon peel — topped with sliced almonds.
ingredients: ¼ cup confectioners' sugar (optional, for dusting)
½ cup (2 oz) sliced almonds (optional, for topping)
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, ground almonds, baking powder, salt and cinnamon with a wire whisk.
In a large bowl cream butter and sugar with an electric mixer; add egg yolks, vanilla and almond extracts; beat at medium speed until light and fluffy.
Add flour mixture; blend at low speed until just combined. Do not overmix.
Roll dough into 1½-inch balls; place 2 inches apart on ungreased baking sheet.
Press an indentation in the center of each ball with your index finger.
Bake 22–24 minutes or until just golden brown on the bottom; transfer to a cool surface.
Combine jam and grated lemon peel in a small bowl; place a teaspoon of filling in the center of each cooled cookie.
Dust with confectioners' sugar and place a few sliced almonds in the jam if desired.
tips: Lemon peel in the jam brightens the flavor — don't skip it.
Make the indentation deep enough to hold a full teaspoon of jam without overflowing.

recipes.name: Pineapple Pocket Pies
recipes.description: Whole-wheat dough logs filled with a cooked pineapple-apricot filling, then sliced and baked — naturally sweetened pocket pies.
ingredients: ¼ cup light brown sugar, firmly packed
½ cup fresh or canned unsweetened pineapple chunks (filling)
instructions: Combine all-purpose flour, whole wheat flour and baking soda in a medium bowl; mix with a wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl cream butter and brown sugar; add honey, egg and vanilla; beat until smooth; scrape bowl.
Add flour mixture; blend at low speed until just combined. Do not overmix.
Gather dough; divide in half; roll into two 6-inch cylinders; wrap tightly in plastic; refrigerate 1 hour.

For the filling: combine apricots, pineapple, brown sugar and water in a saucepan over medium-low heat; stir until sugar dissolves; simmer, stirring occasionally, until mixture thickens. Cool, then purée in a food processor.
Preheat oven to 325°F; roll each cylinder out to 12 inches long on a floured board to a 5-by-18-inch rectangle about ¼ inch thick.
Spread half of the filling in a 2-inch-wide ribbon down the center of the dough.
Using a metal spatula, fold each side lengthwise over the filling, one side overlapping the other by ½ inch.
Cut each strip in half widthwise; transfer to ungreased baking sheets with seam-side down.
Bake 20–22 minutes or until dough turns light gold. Do not brown. Cool 1 minute; transfer; slice when at room temperature.
tips: Roll the filled log carefully — the purée filling can be sticky; use a spatula to help.
Slice after fully cooled with a thin, sharp knife to get clean cuts.

recipes.name: Refrigerator Thumbprint Fudgy Cookies
recipes.description: No-bake fudgy chocolate oat cookies chilled in the refrigerator with a raspberry jam center dusted in powdered sugar.
instructions: In a 2-quart saucepan combine butter, cream and sugar; warm over medium heat until sugar dissolves.
Remove from heat; add vanilla and chocolate chips one cup at a time, stirring after each addition until fully melted.
Fold in oats; stir until all ingredients are thoroughly combined.
Shape dough into 1-inch balls; place on a waxed-paper-lined cookie sheet.
Using the bottom of a glass, flatten each cookie to 2 inches in diameter.
Make a depression in the center of each cookie with your thumb.
Chill in the refrigerator 30 minutes or until set.
Spoon ½ teaspoon of raspberry preserves into the center of each cookie.
Dust with confectioners' sugar.
tips: Add chocolate chips one cup at a time — the residual heat melts them evenly without re-heating.
These don't need an oven — the chocolate and oats set up firm in the refrigerator.

recipes.name: Apple Cream Pennies
recipes.description: Tiny marble-sized cookies sandwiched with a cream cheese and apple butter filling — two bites of pure comfort.
ingredients: 1 cup dark brown sugar, firmly packed
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda and salt; mix with a wire whisk; set aside.
Blend sugars in a large bowl with an electric mixer at medium speed; add butter and mix to form a grainy paste; scrape bowl.
Add eggs and vanilla; beat at medium speed until light and fluffy.
Add flour mixture; blend at low speed until just combined. Do not overmix.
Shape dough into marble-sized balls; place on ungreased baking sheets 1 inch apart.
Bake 10–11 minutes. Do not brown; transfer to a cool surface.
For the filling: blend cream cheese and sugar with electric mixer until smooth; add apple butter; beat until thoroughly combined.
Spread 1 teaspoon of apple cream on the bottom of each cooled cookie; top with another cookie to create a sandwich.
tips: Marble-sized means truly small — these are petite sandwich cookies, not full-sized.
The apple butter filling can be made ahead and refrigerated for up to 3 days.

recipes.name: Jessica's Marshmallow Clouds
recipes.description: Stiff chocolate cookie dough wrapped around frozen miniature marshmallows — they puff up into delightful cloud-like cookies.
ingredients: 1 cup light brown sugar, firmly packed
2 cups (12 oz) miniature semisweet chocolate chips
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F; keep marshmallows in the freezer until the moment you need them.
In a medium bowl combine flour, cocoa and baking soda; set aside.
Combine sugars in a large bowl; blend in butter with electric mixer; scrape bowl; add eggs and vanilla; beat until light and fluffy.
Add flour mixture and chocolate chips; blend at low speed until combined. Batter will be very stiff.
Take 4–5 frozen marshmallows in your palm; cover with a heaping tablespoon of dough; wrap dough around the marshmallows to completely encase them; form a 2-inch ball.
Place on ungreased baking sheets 2 inches apart.
Bake 8–10 minutes; cool on pan 2 minutes, then transfer to a cool flat surface.
tips: Marshmallows must stay frozen until they go in the oven — the warmth of your hands will start melting them; work quickly.
The marshmallow center melts during baking and creates a soft, pillowy interior.

recipes.name: Surprise-Filled Cookies
recipes.description: Vanilla cookie balls with a secret jam center hidden inside — the surprise reveals itself on first bite.
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour and baking powder; mix with a wire whisk; set aside.
In a medium bowl cream butter and sugar with an electric mixer; add egg and vanilla; beat on medium until smooth.
Add flour mixture; blend at low speed until thoroughly combined. Dough will be firm.
Scoop tablespoonfuls of dough; roll into 1-inch-diameter balls; place on ungreased sheets 1 inch apart.
Using the small end of a melon baller, scoop out the center of each ball — do not scoop all the way through.
Place 1½ teaspoons of jam in the scooped-out center; return the removed dough to the mixing bowl for future balls.
Bake 22–24 minutes or until light golden brown; transfer to a cool flat surface.
tips: Use the melon baller's smaller scoop for a neat cavity.
Press the removed dough back into the ball to cover the jam if it peaks out — the surface should look smooth.

recipes.name: Peanut Butter Cream-Filled Cookies
recipes.description: Oat and cinnamon cookies sandwiched with a creamy peanut butter filling — lightly fluted and very satisfying.
ingredients: 1 cup light brown sugar, firmly packed
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking soda, cinnamon and oats; mix well with a wire whisk; set aside.
Cream sugar and butter in a large bowl using electric mixer at medium speed; add egg and vanilla; beat until light and creamy.
Add the flour-oat mixture; blend at low speed until just combined. Do not overmix.
Divide dough into two disks; wrap tightly in plastic; chill 1 hour.
Roll each disk to ¼-inch thickness on a floured board; cut with a 2-inch fluted round cookie cutter dipped in flour.
Bake on ungreased sheets ½ inch apart for 13–15 minutes or until bottoms turn light brown; transfer to a cool surface.
For the filling: cream peanut butter and butter together; add half-and-half and vanilla; gradually mix in confectioners' sugar until smooth.
Spread 1 tablespoon of filling on the bottom of a cookie; top with another cookie to form a sandwich.
tips: A fluted cookie cutter gives these an elegant edge that's worth the extra step.
The peanut butter filling will firm up as it sits — make it right before assembling.

recipes.name: Lemon Cream-Filled Cookies
recipes.description: Delicate lemon shortbread rounds filled with a bright lemon cream — cool and refreshing.
ingredients: 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice (about 1 lemon, filling)
instructions: In a medium bowl cream butter with electric mixer at medium speed; add confectioners' sugar; beat until smooth; add lemon extract; beat until light and fluffy.
Add flour and cornstarch; blend at low speed until thoroughly combined.
Gather dough into 2 equal balls; flatten into disks; wrap in plastic; refrigerate 1 hour.
For the filling: beat butter until fluffy; gradually add sugar while beating; add cream, lemon juice and zest; mix until thoroughly blended; refrigerate 15–20 minutes to firm.
Preheat oven to 325°F.
Roll chilled dough on a floured board to ¼-inch thickness; cut circles with a 2-inch cookie cutter; place on ungreased sheets ½ inch apart.
Bake 15–17 minutes or until edges begin to brown; transfer immediately to a cool surface.
When completely cool, spread 1 teaspoon of lemon cream on a cookie; place another cookie on top to form a sandwich.
tips: Cornstarch makes these shortbreads extra tender — it's what sets them apart from standard sugar cookies.
Fresh lemon zest makes the filling pop; dried or extract won't deliver the same bright flavor.

recipes.name: Bull's Eyes
recipes.description: A show-stopping slab bar: chocolate chip cookie dough as the base, with dollops of double-rich chocolate dough on top — the two bake together into a bull's-eye pattern when cut.
ingredients: 1 cup dark brown sugar, packed (base layer)
2 cups (12 oz) semisweet chocolate chips (base layer)
¼ cup unsweetened cocoa powder (chocolate layer)
½ cup dark brown sugar, packed (chocolate layer)
¼ cup plus 2 tbsp white sugar (chocolate layer)
½ cup salted butter, softened (chocolate layer)
1 large egg plus 1 egg yolk (chocolate layer)
1 cup (6 oz) semisweet chocolate chips (chocolate layer)
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F; grease a 9-by-13-inch glass baking dish.
Make the base layer: combine flour, baking soda and salt in a medium bowl with wire whisk.
In a large bowl blend sugars and butter with electric mixer; scrape bowl; add eggs and vanilla; beat until light and fluffy.
Add flour mixture and chocolate chips; mix just until combined.
Press dough evenly into the prepared pan; sprinkle with coconut; set aside.
Make the chocolate layer: combine flour, baking soda, salt and cocoa in a medium bowl with wire whisk.
In a large bowl blend sugars and butter with mixer; scrape bowl; add eggs and vanilla; beat until combined.
Add flour mixture and chocolate chips; blend at low speed. Do not overmix.
Drop the chocolate dough by rounded teaspoonfuls evenly across the base layer to resemble bull's eyes.
Bake 50–60 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean; cool completely before cutting into bars.
tips: Evenly space the chocolate dough dots so every bar gets a bull's eye when sliced.
The long bake time is correct — this is a thick slab bar that needs full heat to cook through.

recipes.name: Creamy Layered Pudding Bar
recipes.description: Flaky cake-flour shortbread cup holding a rich egg-yolk custard with chocolate chips and pecans — chilled and cut into squares.
ingredients: 1 cup (6 oz) miniature semisweet chocolate chips (filling)
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F; grease an 8-by-8-inch baking pan.
Cream butter and sugar in a medium bowl at medium speed; add egg yolk and vanilla; beat until light and fluffy.
Add cake flour and salt; blend at low speed until just combined.
