Turn dough into pan; refrigerate 15 minutes; then press dough to ¼-inch thickness on the bottom and 1 inch up the sides; return to refrigerator while making filling.
For the filling: mix sugar and cornstarch in a small bowl; set aside.
Beat 5 egg yolks in a medium bowl with mixer on medium-high for 5 minutes until light and fluffy.
Add cornstarch-sugar mixture; mix on medium until combined.
Add vanilla, whipping cream, chocolate chips and pecans; blend at low speed until thoroughly combined.
Pour filling into the pastry-lined pan.
Bake 55–60 minutes or until filling is set and golden brown; chill 4 hours or overnight; cut into bars and serve.
tips: Lightly flour your hands before pressing the dough into the pan — it's sticky.
Don't skip the overnight chill; the custard needs time to fully set before cutting.

recipes.name: Granola Date Bars
recipes.description: A granola-oat crust and crumble surrounding a thick, sweet date-coconut filling — naturally wholesome and satisfying.
ingredients: ¾ cup half-and-half or light cream (filling)
2 cups quick oats (not instant, granola base)
1 cup dark brown sugar, firmly packed (granola base)
½ cup salted butter, melted (granola base)
instructions: For the filling: heat dates, coconut and half-and-half in a medium saucepan over medium heat; stir occasionally until mixture boils and thickens, about 15 minutes; remove from heat; stir in vanilla; set aside to cool.
For the granola base: combine oats, flour, brown sugar, baking soda and cinnamon in a medium bowl; mix with a wire whisk; pour melted butter over dry ingredients and stir until thoroughly moistened.
Press about 3 cups of the granola mixture into the bottom of an 8-by-8-inch baking pan; refrigerate 30 minutes to harden.
Preheat oven to 350°F.
Spread the cooled date filling evenly over the chilled granola base.
Sprinkle remaining granola mixture (about ¼ cup) over the date filling.
Bake 25–30 minutes or until the granola topping is slightly browned and crisp; cool to room temperature before cutting into 2-inch squares.
tips: Cook the date-coconut filling until it noticeably thickens — stir often to prevent sticking.
Pressing and chilling the granola base before filling gives it structure to hold the layers.

recipes.name: Triple-Layered Lemon Bars
recipes.description: Three distinct layers — buttery shortbread, cream cheese filling, and silky homemade lemon curd — chilled and dusted with sugar.
ingredients: 8 oz cream cheese, softened (cream cheese filling)
1 tsp pure lemon extract (cream cheese filling)
¼ cup fresh lemon juice (about 2 lemons, lemon curd)
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F.

For the crust: cream butter and confectioners' sugar with electric mixer on high; add vanilla; mix; add flour; mix at low until incorporated; press evenly into the bottom of an 8-by-8-inch pan; refrigerate 30 minutes; prick with fork; bake 30 minutes until golden; cool on rack.
For the cream cheese filling: beat cream cheese and sugar until smooth; add egg and lemon extract; beat until light; cover and refrigerate.

For the lemon curd: blend egg yolks with cornstarch and sugar in a non-aluminum saucepan; place over low heat; slowly whisk in water and lemon juice; increase to medium-low; cook, stirring constantly, until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon; remove from heat; add lemon peel and butter; cool 10 minutes.
Spread cream cheese filling evenly over the cooled shortbread crust.
Spread lemon curd evenly over the cream cheese layer.
Bake 30–40 minutes or until edges turn light golden brown.
Cool to room temperature; chill 1 hour before cutting into bars; dust top with confectioners' sugar.
tips: Use a non-aluminum saucepan for the lemon curd — aluminum reacts with acid and can make it taste metallic.
The curd is ready when it coats the back of a spoon thickly enough to hold a line drawn through it.

recipes.name: Chocolate Chip Butterscotch Bars
recipes.description: Dense, chewy butterscotch bars packed with pecans and semisweet chocolate chips — easy to make and crowd-pleasing.
ingredients: 1 cup dark brown sugar, firmly packed
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F; grease an 8-by-8-inch baking pan.
Combine flour and baking soda in a medium bowl; mix with a wire whisk; set aside.
In a large bowl blend sugar and butter with electric mixer until smooth; scrape bowl.
Add flour mixture, egg and vanilla; beat at medium speed until light and smooth.
Add pecans and chocolate chips; blend at low speed until just combined. Do not overmix.
Transfer batter into the prepared pan; level the top with a rubber spatula.
Bake in center of oven 35–45 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean but center is still soft.
Cool on rack to room temperature; cut with a sharp knife into 1-by-2-inch bars.
tips: The bars are done when the center is set but still has a slight give — overbaking will dry them out.
Cut when fully cooled for clean edges; warm bars crumble.

recipes.name: Peanut Butter & Jelly Squares
recipes.description: A thick slab of PB&J sandwich built in cookie dough — jelly layered over peanut butter between two sheets of rolled dough, baked and cut into squares.
instructions: In a medium bowl combine flour and baking powder; mix with wire whisk; set aside.
In a medium bowl with electric mixer at medium speed, cream butter and sugar to form a grainy paste; add egg and vanilla; mix until smooth; scrape bowl.
Add flour mixture; blend at low speed until thoroughly combined. Dough will be firm.
Divide dough into two equal disks; wrap tightly in plastic; refrigerate 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 325°F; lightly butter a 9-by-13-inch baking pan.
On a floured board, roll each disk to 9-by-13 inches, about ¼ inch thick.
Place one sheet of dough in the bottom and up the sides of the pan; refrigerate 10 minutes.
Spread the jelly evenly over the chilled dough layer; layer the peanut butter evenly on top of the jelly.
Top with the second sheet of dough; press edges to seal.
Bake 25–30 minutes or until dough is golden; cool completely; dust with confectioners' sugar; cut into squares.
tips: Chill the bottom dough layer before adding the filling so it doesn't tear when you spread.
For cleaner squares, score the top with a knife immediately out of the oven, then cut all the way through once cool.
